notes:
A fix release for v2.29.0. Two of them mattered.

THE VOICE DOWNLOAD ASKS FIRST — EVERYWHERE. v2.29.0 added a question the first time you press Listen: the good narrator (a one-time 139 MB download) or your phone's built-in voice. Two ways in never asked — reading a manga aloud, and the Listen button on a series description. Either could start the download with nothing on screen to explain it. Both ask now, and the check moved down into the engine itself, so no screen can spend that download without your say-so — including the ones with no way to ask you, like the notification and the home-screen widget.

NO MORE RESTARTING A FAILED DOWNLOAD ALL NIGHT. If the voice download failed on a weak connection, it started over at every chapter. Leave a book playing overnight and that was thirty attempts. It now tries once when you press play, and again the next time you press play — not at every chapter.

Also in this release:

The light theme works. It was unusable: the background stayed dark behind light-theme text, and labels inside panels were white on white. There's a proper daytime look now — overcast easing to pale water — with the text to match.

Read-along keeps the voice's own words on screen. The page used to drift as a chapter went on until the sentence being spoken was off-screen entirely. It now follows the actual paragraph. And there's a new button while listening: tap it to stop the page following the voice so you can read ahead, tap again and it catches up.

Voice reliability: switching voices after a failure now actually retries instead of staying stuck on the old failure. A voice that downloads but won't start says so instead of silently handing over to your phone's voice. And the narrator name shown on the widget and lock screen updates when the good voice takes over mid-chapter, instead of naming the wrong one for the rest of the chapter.
